Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Proclamation 1284/2023 provides that a digital ID may be locked or disabled by court order. Criminal penalties for ID fraud adjudicated through courts. DPA enforcement notices subject to legal challenge. Formal judicial oversight mechanism exists in law but specific court review procedures are still being operationalized.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited source was only a 2022 draft hosted on a personal blog. The enacted Ethiopian Digital Identification Proclamation No. 1284/2023, confirmed 'In Force' on Ethiopia's Ministry of Justice legal database, provides at Article 20 (Grievance and Complaint Redressal) that a party dissatisfied with a decision of the ID Institution may petition the courts for judicial review of that decision — an ID-specific judicial mechanism rather than merely general oversight. This meets the scale's code 3 ('Yes, with ID-specific judicial mechanisms'); upgraded from 2.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Fayda is a live, operational MOSIP-based biometric digital ID system under Proclamation 1284/2023. As of early 2026, ~29.5 million enrolled out of ~130 million population; 91 agencies integrated; real-time authentication and eKYC operational. System is multi-purpose foundational ID but not yet at universal coverage.

At roughly a third of Ethiopia's ~130 million population enrolled, the system is clearly operational and multi-agency but not yet nationwide/universal, so 'Partially deployed' (code 4) remains the correct score; the comment's 29.5m/91-agency figures are now superseded and should be refreshed.

Comments: Eligible from age 5 and above for all residents. Children below 5 are planned for a special registration program. As of 2026, Fayda ID required for school registration for Grade 1+. Biometric data collected for all eligible ages. Younger children (below 5) not yet covered by the system.
